group.passage: The thin plastic bag that carries groceries home is so ordinary that most people never stop to think about it. Yet the bag is younger than many of the shoppers who use it, and its short history shows how quickly a clever idea can become a worldwide problem. The story begins in a chemical plant. In 1933, chemists in Northwich, England, discovered by accident the first method of making polyethylene that was practical for industry. Polyethylene is now the most widely used plastic on Earth, but it was first put to use in secret by the British military during the Second World War. The shopping bag came more than thirty years later. In 1965, the Swedish company Celloplast patented a one-piece polyethylene bag designed by its engineer Sten Gustaf Thulin. Once it appeared, the new bag spread with remarkable speed. By 1979, plastic bags made up 80 percent of the bag market in Europe. In 1982, two major American supermarket chains, Safeway and Kroger, switched from paper to plastic, and other stores soon followed. By the end of the 1980s, plastic had almost completely replaced paper at checkout counters around the world. At the same time, as the chart shows, factories were turning out more and more plastic of every kind. The success, however, came at a high price. Thrown-away bags have since been found everywhere from the deep ocean to the top of Mount Everest. In 1997, a sailor and researcher named Charles Moore came across a huge area of floating plastic waste in the Pacific Ocean, now known as the Great Pacific Garbage Patch. In 2002, after thin plastic bags were found to have blocked drains during terrible floods, Bangladesh became the first country to ban them. This proved to be only a beginning: by July 2018, a United Nations review of 192 countries found that 127 had some kind of national law on plastic bags. By 2019, the world was producing about 460 million tonnes of plastic a year, around 230 times as much as in 1950. The shopping bag, once seen as a simple convenience, has become a symbol of a much larger problem. It reminds us that the true cost of an invention may take decades to appear.

translation_zh.text:
塑膠袋的興起與代價

把雜貨提回家的薄塑膠袋太普通了，大多數人從來不會停下來想到它。然而這種袋子比許多使用它的購物者還要年輕，而它短短的歷史顯示，一個聰明的點子可以多快變成全世界的問題。

故事從一座化學工廠開始。1933 年，英格蘭諾斯威治的化學家意外發現了第一種在工業上可行的聚乙烯製造方法。聚乙烯如今是地球上使用最廣的塑膠，但它最初是在第二次世界大戰期間被英國軍方祕密使用。購物袋則是三十多年後才出現。1965 年，瑞典公司 Celloplast 為該公司工程師斯滕‧古斯塔夫‧圖林設計的一體成形聚乙烯袋取得專利。

這種新袋子一出現，就以驚人的速度普及。到了 1979 年，塑膠袋已占歐洲袋子市場的百分之八十。1982 年，美國兩家大型連鎖超市 Safeway 和 Kroger 從紙袋改用塑膠袋，其他商店也很快跟進。到了 1980 年代末，全世界的結帳櫃台上，塑膠袋幾乎已經完全取代了紙袋。同時，如圖表所示，工廠生產的各種塑膠越來越多。

然而，這樣的成功付出了很高的代價。從那以後，從深海到聖母峰頂，到處都發現過被丟棄的塑膠袋。1997 年，一位名叫查爾斯‧摩爾的水手兼研究者，在太平洋上遇到一大片漂浮的塑膠垃圾，也就是現在所稱的「太平洋垃圾帶」。2002 年，在薄塑膠袋被發現在嚴重水災期間堵塞排水溝之後，孟加拉成為第一個禁用薄塑膠袋的國家。這後來證明只是個開始：到了 2018 年 7 月，聯合國對 192 個國家的一項調查發現，有 127 國訂有某種管制塑膠袋的全國性法律。

到了 2019 年，全世界每年生產約 4 億 6 千萬公噸的塑膠，大約是 1950 年的 230 倍。曾被視為簡單便利品的購物袋，已成為一個大得多的問題的象徵。它提醒我們，一項發明真正的代價，可能要好幾十年才會顯現。

1965 年瑞典 Celloplast 為工程師 Sten Gustaf Thulin 設計的一體成形聚乙烯袋取得專利（f3；UNEP 1965 條）
1979 年塑膠袋占歐洲袋子市場 80%（f4；UNEP 1979 條）
1982 年 Safeway、Kroger 從紙袋改用塑膠袋，其他商店跟進（f5；UNEP 1982 條 two of the biggest supermarket chains；選文寫 two major，未誇大）
1980 年代末塑膠袋幾乎完全取代全世界的紙袋（f6；UNEP：By the end of the decade … almost entirely replaced paper bags around the world）
塑膠袋從深海到聖母峰頂都有發現（f7）
1997 年水手兼研究者 Charles Moore 發現太平洋垃圾帶（f8；UNEP 1997 條）
2002 年孟加拉在薄塑膠袋於嚴重水災時堵塞排水溝後，成為第一個禁用薄塑膠袋的國家（f9；UNEP 2002 條）
2018 年 7 月聯合國（UNEP）檢視 192 國，127 國有某種全國性塑膠袋法律（f10；UNEP 2018 條）
